title: Find faster, write with less friction
summary: Find the right note, jump to text inside it, make a copy and understand earlier versions more easily.

items: Search using several words or an exact phrase in quotes, with matching text highlighted in note titles and search previews. Choose a folder or view to narrow where you search.
Use compact search filters to look in titles or content, show pinned notes or find notes with reminders. Clear the filters whenever you want the full view back.
Press Ctrl+F or use the search button in an open note to find text, move between matches and optionally match letter case. Find works in reading and editing modes.
Duplicate a note from its right-click menu. The copy keeps its content and folder, with its own dates and no copied reminders, pins or history.
Compare an earlier note version with the current text side by side. Highlights show what belongs to each version before you choose to restore it.
A small, dismissible tip explains Ctrl-click, Shift-click and dragging to select several notes, then right-clicking for actions.

Clearer keyboard focus and improved menu navigation make it easier to use Scribe without a mouse. Open note actions with Shift+F10, move through menus with the arrow keys and close the active control with Escape.
Markdown formatting and list continuation now use the editor’s undo history. Switching between reading and editing keeps the same text editor in place.
Pasted Markdown keeps its spacing and code indentation while Windows line endings are normalized consistently. Inside fenced code blocks, Tab and Shift+Tab indent or unindent code.

Escape closes the open folder menu first, then keeps nonempty work as a draft before closing the new-note composer. Find closes before leaving edit mode, and keyboard focus stays inside the open composer.
Caret scrolling avoids measuring the rest of a long note after the current line, reducing unnecessary work while typing.
